key_insight: Deep truncated FBSDEs stabilize high-dimensional PDE solving by decoupling strongly coupled forward-backward dynamics with gradient truncation, fictitious-play averaging, and a pathwise consistency shortcut.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more robust neural solver for convection-dominated and strongly coupled PDE/FBSDE systems where standard deep solvers can become unstable in high dimensions.
method: Gradient-truncated iterative decoupling separates forward and backward updates while preserving coupled dynamics.
Fictitious-play averaging reduces unstable feedback from parameter-dependent forward paths during optimization.
A pathwise consistency term adds local gradient shortcuts to help mitigate vanishing gradients.
evidence_signal: The paper reports numerical experiments showing improved accuracy and stability on both low- and high-dimensional problems, including strongly coupled cases, plus a residual-based error estimate and conditional convergence result.
watch_item: Performance and convergence depend on suitable conditions, and the pathwise consistency loss may be omitted in theory but still requires careful tuning in practice.
paper_title: Deep Truncated FBSDE Method: A Robust Solver for High-Dimensional Nonlinear PDEs and Fully Coupled FBSDEs
